messages.text:
Conditionally created dialog in a fragment stops logically existing after rerun of a fragment while still existing on the website

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

When a fragment gets rerun and it has conditionally rendered child dialog (for example guarded by a button being clicked) the dialog will stop being responsive while still existing on the page

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st


@st.dialog("Dialog", dismissible=False)
def show_dialog() -> None:
    if st.button("Increment"):
        st.session_state["clicks"] = st.session_state.get("clicks", 0) + 1
    st.write("Clicks:", st.session_state.get("clicks", 0))


@st.fragment(run_every=5)
def parent_fragment() -> None:
    st.session_state["parent_runs"] = st.session_state.get("parent_runs", 0) + 1
    st.write("Parent runs:", st.session_state["parent_runs"])
    if st.button("Open dialog"):
        show_dialog()


st.write("Open the dialog, then wait for the parent fragment's next automatic rerun (every 5 seconds).")
parent_fragment()
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Click Open dialog
2. start clicking increment
3. after parent reruns the dialog stops being responsive and streamlit will log The fragment with id <id> does not exist anymore - it might have been removed during a preceding full-app rerun.

### Expected Behavior

The dialog to still be responsive

### Current Behavior

The dialog stops being responsive

### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.64.0
- Python version: Python 3.13.13
- Operating System: Linux 7.1.4-arch1-1
- Browser: Firefox


### Additional Information

worked when ran with
```
uv run --no-project --with streamlit==1.57.0 streamlit run repro.py
```
stopped working at
```
uv run --no-project --with streamlit==1.58.0 streamlit run repro.py
```

evidence.text:
## Defining and calling a fragment

Streamlit provides a decorator ([`st.fragment`](/develop/api-reference/execution-flow/st.fragment)) to turn any function into a fragment function. When you call a fragment function that contains a widget function, a user triggers a _fragment rerun_ instead of a full rerun when they interact with that fragment's widget. During a fragment rerun, only your fragment function is re-executed. Anything within the main body of your fragment is updated on the frontend, while the rest of your app remains the same. We'll describe fragments written across multiple containers later on.

Here is a basic example of defining and calling a fragment function. Just like with caching, remember to call your function after defining it.

```python
import streamlit as st

@st.fragment
def fragment_function():
    if st.button("Hi!"):
        st.write("Hi back!")

fragment_function()
```

If you want the main body of your fragment to appear in the sidebar or another container, call your fragment function inside a context manager.

```python
with st.sidebar:
    fragment_function()
```

evidence.title: Rerun() inside an st.fragment resets widget values to defaults.
evidence.text:
### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

@st.fragment()
def toggle_and_text():
    if st.button("rerun"):
        st.rerun()
    t = st.text_input("Enter t:",value='foo', key='t')
    st.info(f't = {t}')

toggle_and_text()
st.header('Outside Fragment')
st.info(f'session_state_t = {st.session_state.t}')
st.button("Update")
```

evidence.title: Rerun() inside an st.fragment resets widget values to defaults.

### Additional Information

_No response_

Hey [USER] Thank you for the issue! I believe this is an expected behavior. Widgets that don't appear in the run are deleted. Here's what's happening:

1. Text is updated in string
2. Button is pressed and rerun occurs (but the the text was never rendered. Widget is reset
3. Widget reverts back to default

If you move the rerun button _after_ the text input. Everything works as expected. If you want it before the text input, you can leverage `st.empty()` like in this example:

```python
import streamlit as st

@st.fragment()
def toggle_and_text():
    foo = st.empty()
    t = st.text_input("Enter t:",value='foo', key='t')
    st.info(f't = {t}')
    if foo.button("rerun"):
        st.rerun()

toggle_and_text()
st.header('Outside Fragment')
st.info(f'session_state_t = {st.session_state.t}')
st.button("Update")
```

I'll probably close this issue, but feel free to ask any questions
